gap: No rival result ChatGPT got states that both flight-legal AC power banks it recommends, the Goal Zero Sherpa 100AC and the Omnicharge Omni 20+, have modified-sine outlets according to their own makers. That goes against ChatGPT's own advice to buy pure sine. The $119 BLUETTI Elite 10 Mini is pure sine and is rated 3,000+ cycles to 80%, while Goal Zero rates the Sherpa only for 'Hundreds of Cycles' and doesn't say to what capacity.
standout_why: I opened geekchamp, thunderboltlaptop and Engadget, and the current Dealectric page. geekchamp states no waveform for any product. It only tells readers to 'look for pure sine wave output', and for the Sherpa it gives 95 Wh and no AC figure. thunderboltlaptop states no waveform, no usable energy and no continuous rating for its six generic 27,000 mAh banks, and says it did not test them. Engadget gives the Sherpa's 25,600 mAh / 95 Wh but no AC wattage or waveform. ChatGPT's answer said 'Look for a model with a pure sine wave AC inverter' and then recommended the Sherpa first. Our old page already says 'modified sine' for the Sherpa and the Omni 20+, but it has no cycle-life comparison and leaves the Elite 10 Mini out.
decides: It confirms the Sherpa 100AC or Omni 20+ for a laptop on a plane. A laptop's own power brick normally runs fine on modified sine, so a Sherpa buyer loses nothing. But a shopper who follows ChatGPT's pure-sine advice, or who plugs in a CPAP machine or anything motorised, can't get pure sine in the under-100 Wh class from either maker. Their maker-sourced option is the Elite 10 Mini: pure sine, 128 Wh, LiFePO4, rated 3,000+ cycles to 80%, $119 on 2026-11-14. That's less than half the Sherpa's roughly $250, which comes from our old page; I couldn't re-check it today. The catch is that it's over 100 Wh and won't fly as a normal carry-on. The table footnote: '100 W' on the Sherpa is a maximum (110 V × 0.9 A, about 99 W), not a stated continuous rating, and none of these makers publishes a surge figure.

findings.label: AC outlet waveform and rating
findings.value: Modified sine wave; 110 V, up to 0.9 A (100 W max), 60 Hz
findings.source_title: GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC Guia Del Usuario – Technical Specifications (manualslib copy of the Goal Zero manual)
findings.note: goalzero.com returned HTTP 429. The official Shopify-CDN PDF wouldn't extract, so this is a third-party copy of the maker's manual. 110 V × 0.9 A = 99 W. The '100 W' is a maximum, not a continuous rating, and the manual lists no surge figure. The manual lists LG Chem 18650 cells, which may mean it's the pre-2022 version, not the 'New Sherpa 100AC'.

findings.label: Capacity basis and cycle life
findings.value: 25,600 mAh @ 3.7 V (= 94.7 Wh); Li-ion NMC; 'Hundreds of Cycles' (no end-of-life capacity stated)
findings.source_title: GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC Guia Del Usuario – Technical Specifications
findings.note: 25,600 mAh × 3.7 V = 94.72 Wh. This explains why sources say both 94.7 Wh and 95 Wh (Engadget rounds to 95 Wh). The manual also gives 2.2 lb (985 g).

findings.label: AC wattage and waveform as stated by a cited rival
findings.value: Engadget lists '25,600 mAh, 95Wh' and gives no AC wattage or waveform
findings.source_title: The best laptop power banks for 2026 (Engadget)
findings.note: Cited by ChatGPT in two chats. Engadget's MacBook Pro test (6% to 72% in 1h 21m) used USB-C, not the AC outlet.

findings.label: AC outlet waveform and capacity
findings.note: Quotes: 'Omnicharge adopting a type known as a modified sine wave' and 'The capacity of Omni 20+ (20400mAh/71Wh)'. The FAQ also lists a 150 V HVDC mode alongside 120 V AC. The 100 W AC figure is on the product page, which returned HTTP 429 today.

findings.label: Capacity, AC rating, waveform, cycle life, price
findings.value: 128 Wh LiFePO4; 200 W AC; pure sine wave; 3,000+ cycles to 80%; $119.00 (BLUETTI US, 2026-11-14)
findings.note: Price and cycle line come from storecheck product (Shopify JSON) and the page itself. 'Pure Sine Wave' appears only in the page's image alt text because the Tech Specs block rendered empty. The page lists no surge or Power Lifting figure. 128 Wh is over 100 Wh.

findings.value: geekchamp gives no waveform for any of its 10 products and lists the Daran's '200W peak' next to a 100 W limit. thunderboltlaptop gives no waveform for any of its 6 products and labels none of its AC ratings as continuous.
findings.source_title: Best AC-Outlet Power Banks: Sherpa 100AC vs Mini Power Stations (geekchamp)
